content: 1. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 3. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 4. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 5. Both fosamprenavir and abacavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 6. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, the abemaciclib dose should be increased to the level prior to the initiation of the inhibitor. 7. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 8. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. New-onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. 9. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 10. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. The cytotoxic component DM1 is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase DM1 exposure and toxicity. 11. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of albiglutide through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 12. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 13. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 15. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 16. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 17. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 18. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 19. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 20. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 21. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 22. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 23. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of amoxapine by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 24. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 25. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, potentially reducing their therapeutic effects. 26. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 27. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 28. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Conversely, fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting the same enzyme. The clinical significance of these interactions is currently unknown. 29. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 30. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 31. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 32. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If atorvastatin is used, limit the dose to 20 mg/day. 33. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 34. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of avapritinib. 35. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of axitinib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 36. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 37. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, limit co-administration to less than 14 consecutive days. 38. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of fosamprenavir. 39. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 40. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 41. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 42. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 43. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bosutinib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 44. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored for adverse reactions. 45. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Administer half the usual dose of brexpiprazole when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also co-administered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the usual dose. 46. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by 50%. 47. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of bromocriptine by inhibiting its metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 48. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing the same enzyme. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 49. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of buprenorphine by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration may increase toxicity, and close monitoring is recommended. 50. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of buprenorphine buccal by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration may increase toxicity, and close monitoring is recommended. 51. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of buprenorphine subdermal implant by inhibiting its metabolism. Patients should be monitored for signs of overmedication. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary. 52. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inhibiting its metabolism. Patients transitioning from transmucosal buprenorphine co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored for toxicity. Transition back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments if toxicity occurs. 53. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 54. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 55. Butalbital decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 56. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of cabazitaxel by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration may increase toxicity, and close monitoring is recommended. Avoid co-administration if possible.
